questions.learningObjective: Solve a quantitative radioactive decay and half-life problem by applying the governing physical principle.
questions.stem: A nuclide has half-life 5 days and a sample contains 400 nuclei. What is its activity in decays per day?

options.misconception: Uses the decay constant where the half-life is required
Divides the nucleus count by the half-life directly
Multiplies the decay constant by the half-life an extra time

questions.explanation: Activity is A = lambda times N, where lambda = ln(2)/T = ln(2)/5 = 0.1386 per day. Thus A = 5.55 × 10^1 decays per day. Dividing N by T ignores the ln(2) factor, multiplying N by T is dimensionally wrong, and lambda times T times N double-counts the half-life.
questions.hint: Compute lambda = ln(2)/T, then multiply by the number of nuclei.
